Alright, let's start with a little background about me: I love strategy, mostly RTS, games but barely have any experience with 4X games. I was intimidated at first with the interface of the game when I saw it first back in 2015 with all those units, capital ships, and such. Now, for some reason, it was on my recommended list and after playing Starcraft II, I was in to anything Sci-fi. So, with a discount, I bought the game and, oh boy, how wrong was I about the game.

If you have any experience with any sort of RTS like Starcraft, Command and Conquer, etc., then starting off might be smoother but that does not mean that it will be heavily demanding to new players in general. While the tutorials are lackluster, the gameplay is a new story, having so much breadth and depth to it. There are three races, the TEC (humans | specialize generally in cheap and fast unit production while maintaining their strengths), the Advent (a humanoid race | specialize in expensive but powerful units with great shields), and the Vasari (a humanoid alien race | specialize in unique ships that have special traits that are not accessible to TEC and Advent such as semi-shield piercing) in the vanilla game, with each having two more 'sub-races' (the Rebels and Loyalists), making a total of 6 factions to choose from, each having their specialities and weaknesses. For example, a TEC (the human race) Rebels (one of the two sub-races) may look exactly similar to its counterpart, the TEC Loyalists, but are more agressive in general as opposed to the more defensive Loyalists. It has the "tech trees" of a 4X game where one can pick specializations in either making allies and forming peace treaties to conquering the star system.

In terms of fleet building, things can get quite interesting. One starts off with a small fleet, as there are fleet limits. However, as one gathers more resources, one can increase the fleet limit to another level, allowing more ship production until the very limit (but to be honest, 99% of the time it feels like you'll be building infinity ships at the end game). Same goes for Capital Ships (basically act like 'Hero units' of your fleet). However, one just build ships of one time and then dominate the galaxy; each ship has their own specializations. For example, there are Colony Ships (either Capital or otherwise) that are needed to colonize planets in order to expand territory, as well as support ships that increase the capability of your fleet but are useless when alone. In short, fleet building offers a great variety of playstyle to any player in addition to the different factions. Another great thing is that once you have massive space battles happening with possibly 200 ships of two warring factions having a face off, you can turn on cinematic mode and toggle off the UI and sit back, relax, and enjoy the lightshow.

I have not covered everything in depth, as there are more components to the game e.g. Culture, Diplomacy, Fleet Compositions, etc., but they are not needed as much for a new player, as well as keeping the review short.

There are also DLCs and Mods to add to your gaming experience of Sins of a Solar Empire: Rebellion. Currently, there are 4 DLCs that you can buy to add to your game, each adding some sort of variety such as new planets, stars, etc. You may have noticed that this game does not support a Steam Worshop, but there are actually available mods in this game available in other websites with a simple google search. Personally, I enjoy the vanilla experience, but I occasionally put on mods such as Thrawn's Revenge: Ascendancy to keep the game fresh and enjoyable.

Overall, I love this game to bits and I really reccommend it to anyone looking for a new game to play. It may not be for everyone and it has its weaknesses such as slight repetitiveness (but that's the problem many Strategy games are facing anyway), little micro (if you're into that thing, but there is micro involved in harder difficulty settings), and such but there are plenty of things to enjoy about this game. I know this review is quite long so I'll end it here and let the game do the talking if you decide to give it a shot. Thanks for reading and have fun gaming!
